title: Tabletop SLO Experiments and Customer Impact Mapping Initiative - 2026
content:
Purpose:

This is a cross-functional project plan to run a series of tabletop experiments that connect SLO design choices to concrete customer-impact signals. Goal is to reduce ambiguity when teams choose SLO targets, create repeatable experiment templates, validate fallback policies, and produce measurable handoffs for product and support.

Context and motivation:
- We have many SLO adoption artifacts, but teams still struggle to translate an abstract SLO (e.g., p95 latency <= 250ms) into business impact and runbook thresholds.
- Incidents show we often notice regressions by engineering telemetry, not by customer-facing signals. That latency in detection has cost (support escalations, churn risk, internal firefighting).
- Tabletop experiments help us proactively validate: monitoring coverage, escalation triggers, and the customer-visible behaviors when SLOs are breached.

Scope:
- Pilot scope: three services representing different workloads and user expectations: hosted-api (low-latency public API), model-serving-dedicated (predictable throughput), and private-edge-gateway (regional/private deployment).
- Run 4 tabletop scenarios per service: traffic spike, degraded storage backend, KV cache corruption, and multi-region failover.
- Produce: experiment report, runbook changes, new synthetic customer probes, and a mapped set of customer-impact metrics.
- Out of scope: wholesale SLO redefinition across org; this is an experimentation and validation effort with recommended follow-ups.

Objectives (SMART):
1) Within 8 weeks, run 12 tabletop exercises and deliver a one-page experiment report per exercise.
2) Identify at least 3 observable customer-impact signals per service (error page rate, async job backlog growth, UX latency percentiles) and wire them into the alerting cadence.
3) For each service, create a minimal runbook update that maps an SLO degradation to an operational play with escalation steps and a suggested communication template.

Participants and responsibilities:
- Initiative lead: Elena Park (coordination, outcome synthesis, exec brief)
- SRE facilitators: Marcus Chen, Priya Singh (tabletop creation, metrics instrumentation checklist)
- Service owners/product owners: (assigned per pilot) Liam O'Connor (hosted-api), Sofia Alvarez (model-serving-dedicated), Diego Ramirez (private-edge-gateway)
- Observability: telemetry engineer (instrumentation, synthetic probes)
- Support & CS: 1 representative per service for customer-impact interpretation and comms templating
- Engineering on-call: 2 engineers per service for exercise participation

High-level timeline (8-week cadence):
- Week 0: Kickoff, scenario selection, baseline metric capture (create baseline dashboards).
- Week 1-2: Instrumentation tweaks and synthetic probe setup.
- Week 3-6: Run tabletop exercises (1 service per week, with 4 scenarios each; schedule two half-day sessions per service).
- Week 7: Synthesize results, update runbooks, and produce exec one-pager.
- Week 8: Review with product and support, decide go/no-go for wider rollouts.

Experiment design (per tabletop):
1) Hypothesis: short, falsifiable. Example: "If p95 latency increases above 350ms for 10 minutes, then error page rate rises by >0.5% and support tickets increase within 60 minutes."
2) Pre-conditions: baseline SLO values, active synthetic traffic, observer on-call present, support rep listening in, incident commander assigned.
3) Injected failure (non-destructive): simulate backend latency using circuit breaker toggle, or reduce cache hit-rate via feature flag.
4) Observable signals to track: telemetry (p50/p95/p99), request error rate, downstream queue depth, synthetic customer probe success, support mention rate (Slack keyword), number of failing integrations.
5) Communication & escalation flow: timeline of alerts, who calls a war room, customer comms cadence (15/30/60/120 minute updates).
6) Success criteria: defined detection, correct escalation, and measurable customer-impact mapping (e.g., observed support ticket surge = predicted).

Measurement plan and customer-impact mapping:
- For each service we will produce a small table (SLO metric -> customer signal -> threshold -> action). Example: 
  - SLO: p95 latency > 350ms (10min window)
  - Customer signal: synthetic checkout failure rate > 2% (5min)
  - Action: page SRE, post to #prod-incident, throttle non-critical traffic, open high-priority webhook to CS.
- Map signals to customer personas: end-user (frontend latency, error page), integrator (webhook retries, queue backlog), enterprise admin (billing lag, policy failures).
- Tag severity with impact buckets: low (cosmetic), medium (reduced throughput for some users), high (major revenue paths affected).

Runbook template (minimal required fields):
- Condition/Trigger: what metric crossed and for how long.
- Immediate mitigation steps: quick rollback, traffic re-route, disable experimental feature.
- Triage questions: affected regions, affected models, cache state, storage errors.
- Escalation matrix: on-call -> SRE lead -> Product TPM -> Engineering manager -> Exec.
- Customer comms: initial acknowledgement message + suggested 3 later updates.
- Postmortem checklist: data collection window, preserve traces, tag alerts, timeline reconstruction.

Communication plan and stakeholder alignment:
- Weekly working sync (30m) during pilot, attendees: participants above + product and CS leads.
- Slack channel: #reliability-experiments for real-time play-by-play.
- Exec snapshot: 1-page with recommended policy changes and risk heatmap.
- Confluence page: canonical experiment templates and filled reports (linked above).

Artifacts to deliver per exercise:
- One-page experiment report (synthesized findings and runbook diffs).
- Dashboards with annotated baseline and injected periods.
- Snippets for alert rule changes (prometheus/metrics DSL).
- Communication templates saved to shared resume folder for Support.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: experiments leak into production traffic and cause real harm. Mitigation: synthetic isolates, canary namespaces, abort criteria, pre-approved rollback steps.
- Risk: lack of observability for business signals (billing, support). Mitigation: instrument lightweight counters, add synthetic probes that emulate paid flows.
- Risk: no-shows from product/support. Mitigation: pre-book calendar slots, require RSVP, include asynchronous readouts if absent.

Success criteria for the pilot:
- We ran >= 10 exercises and each produced a one-page report.
- For each service, at least one runbook change was merged and deployed to the handbook.
- At least 2 alert rules were modified to include customer-probe correlation.
- Product and CS signoff on at least one comms template per service.

Follow-ups and rollouts:
- If successful, expand playbook to 6 additional services in Q2 and bake the experiment template into SRE onboarding.
- Create a "SLO Tabletop" checklist in the release gate for high-risk launches.

Meeting notes snapshot (working):
- 2026-02-11 Kickoff: product asked us to prioritize hosted-api and to include billing-latency metrics.
- 2026-02-18 Observability sync: telemetry engineer flagged missing synthetic probes for private-edge-gateway; added TODO.
- 2026-02-24 Draft runbooks circulated; comments requested by 2026-03-01.

To do (owner tagged):
- [Elena] finalize exec one-pager template by 2026-02-15.
- [Marcus] create synthetic probe harness (declarative job) by 2026-02-22.
- [Priya] create dashboard baseline panels and share with service owners by 2026-02-25.
- [Liam / Sofia / Diego] RSVP and assign 2 on-call engineers for their service exercises by 2026-02-16.

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments short and tightly scoped; avoid multi-failure chaos in pilot.
- Record all sessions and store in the confluence page.
- We should capture a short customer-impact video clip (screen capture of synthetic checkout) for exec brief.

Appendix A — example one-page experiment report (template):
- Title / date / facilitator / participants
- Hypothesis (1 line)
- Setup (what was instrumented; traffic levels)
- Inject (what changed)
- Timeline of observable signals (visuals attached)
- Key findings (3 bullets)
- Runbook diffs (what to change)
- Next steps and owners

Appendix B — quick comms template (initial ack):
"We are investigating increased latency affecting some API requests. Our engineering team has identified a degraded dependency and are executing mitigations. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. If you are impacted, please reply to this message with example request IDs."

Appendix C — quick measurement checklist (for facilitators):
- Confirm synthetic probe active and target traffic same as baseline
- Ensure tracing sampling for the affected service is at 100% for the window
- Confirm support watch channel is connected to incident timeline
- Pre-create temp dashboard with expected metrics

-- end of working draft --

Comments welcome. This is intentionally a practical, low-friction plan to get teams running experiments and translating SLOs into actionable, customer-focused operations.
